hypotheses.statement: Management/marketing view: promotions drove volume growth in FY2025 and are our most effective commercial tool
hypotheses.implication: The case for a 20% budget increase rests on a claim the data do not support

hypotheses.statement: Promotions mostly shift existing demand (from full price and from future weeks) rather than create new volume
hypotheses.implication: Promotional spend is largely subsidising purchases that would have happened anyway

hypotheses.statement: Higher promotional intensity and depth are the main driver of the gross-margin decline
hypotheses.implication: Reducing depth and intensity is the main lever to recover margin; other cost drivers are not yet ruled out (see H6)

hypotheses.statement: Promotion returns differ by category: some categories earn positive incremental margin
hypotheses.implication: The 2026 plan should reallocate by category instead of scaling spend across the board

hypotheses.statement: Extending deep discounts to Household would create value
hypotheses.implication: Household is the worst-returning category; deeper discounts there would amplify losses

hypotheses.statement: The gross-margin decline is mainly driven by non-promotional factors (input costs, mix outside promotions)
hypotheses.implication: Sources contain no cost or mix data; a margin bridge should confirm the promo share of the decline before final budget sign-off
